usdRate.sourceName: Servicio de Impuestos Internos, dólar observado (published by the Banco Central de Chile), 27 October 2026
usdRate.note: CLP 994.29 per US dollar on 27 October 2026 (October average to date 981.58); World Bank 2025 average 951.3.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Instituto Nacional de Estadísticas (INE), IPC September 2026
inflation_cpi.note: CPI rose 0.4% in September 2026, 4.0% so far in 2026 and 4.1% over 12 months (released 8 October 2026). World Bank 2025 average 4.2%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: Banco Central de Chile 3% inflation target over a two-year horizon (reported by Rankia, Oct 2026); CPI 4.1% in September 2026
inflation_projection.note: The central bank's 3% target has a long record of credibility and inflation expectations two years ahead stay near it, so planning uses the target despite the current 4.1% rate.

policy_rate.sourceName: Banco Central de Chile, Informativo diario de operaciones financieras, 30 October 2026 (TPM)
policy_rate.note: Monetary policy rate (TPM) 4.50%, held unanimously at the 27 October 2026 meeting and unchanged since December 2025; next meeting 15 December 2026.

savings_account_rate.note: Bank savings accounts (cuentas de ahorro) in Chile are mostly UF-indexed with a small real rate; no published average rate was found in central bank or CMF statistics that could be read.

fdr_3m_rate.sourceName: Banco Central de Chile, average deposit rates of the financial system, peso operations, 30 to 89 days (Base de Datos Estadísticos)
fdr_3m_rate.note: Average rate on new non-indexed peso term deposits of 30-89 days was 4.12% a year in September 2026 (4.14% in August); deposits of 90 days to 1 year paid 4.53%.

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: Banco Central de Chile, average deposit rates of the financial system, peso operations, 90 days to 1 year (Base de Datos Estadísticos)
fdr_1y_rate.note: Average rate on new peso term deposits of 90 days to 1 year was 4.53% in September 2026; 1-3 year deposits paid 5.26%.

dps_rate.note: No monthly recurring-deposit product with a published rate exists in Chile; regular saving is done through savings accounts, term deposits, mutual funds or voluntary pension savings (APV).

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: Banco Central de Chile, average deposit rates and flows of the financial system, peso operations (weighted by September 2026 flows)
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Weighting the four term buckets by their September 2026 flows (CLP 18.3 trillion at 4.12%, 4.3 trillion at 4.53%, 1.5 trillion at 5.26%, 0.02 trillion at 5.95%) gives about 4.27% a year. World Bank FR.INR.DPST 2024: 6.07%.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: Chile has no government savings certificate or retail savings bond sold directly to individuals; Treasury bonds (BTP/BTU) are auctioned to institutions and bought by individuals only through brokers.

tbill_91d_rate.note: The Treasury issues no bills; the central bank's 30-360 day discount notes (PDBC) are auctioned to banks and institutional investors, and no PDBC 90-day auction was held in late October 2026 (Banco Central de Chile daily bulletin). The 180-day average interbank swap rate was 4.66%.

tbond_5y_rate.sourceName: Banco Central de Chile, Informativo diario de operaciones financieras, 30 October 2026: peso bond rates, 5 years
tbond_5y_rate.note: Secondary-market yield on 5-year peso government bonds (BTP/BCP) was 5.81% on 28 October 2026; 5-year UF-indexed bonds yielded 2.27% real.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Banco Central de Chile, Informativo diario de operaciones financieras, 30 October 2026: peso bond rates, 10 years
tbond_10y_rate.note: Secondary-market yield on 10-year peso government bonds was 6.00% on 28 October 2026 (Trading Economics: 5.98% on 30 October); 10-year UF bonds yielded 2.62% real.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Chile income determination and taxes on personal income (reviewed 30 Oct 2026)
tax_bank_interest.note: No withholding: only real interest (interest less the rise in the cost of living) is added to income and taxed at the progressive Global Complementary Tax rates (0% to 40%); 4% is the bracket rate for a middle earner (taxable income about 13.5-30 UTA a year). Many small savers pay nothing.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: There is no government savings certificate in Chile; government bond interest is taxed like other interest (real interest at progressive rates).

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Dirección de Presupuestos (Ministry of Finance), Informe de Pasivos Contingentes 2025: state guarantee on deposits (Ley 21.130); UF value from the SII
deposit_insurance_limit.note: The state guarantees 100% of term deposits of individuals up to 200 UF per bank per calendar year (400 UF across the system), set by Ley 21.130 of 2019; 200 UF = CLP 8,249,526 at the UF of 41,247.63 on 31 October 2026 (sii.cl).

credit_card_rate_cap.sourceName: Comisión para el Mercado Financiero, Certificado 10/2026 (Diario Oficial 15 Oct 2026): maximum conventional interest rate
credit_card_rate_cap.note: Legal cap (tasa máxima convencional) for non-indexed peso credit of 90 days or more up to 50 UF, the bracket covering most card balances: 41.02% a year (simple annual rate) from 15 October 2026; 47.73% for under 90 days.

equity_return_low.sourceName: Santiago Stock Exchange IGPA index 51,947 on 30 Oct 2026, up about 9% in a year (Trading Economics)
equity_return_low.note: Low case: Chilean shares repeat their flat 2016-2023 decade and earn little more than deposits.

equity_return_base.sourceName: IGPA index history (Trading Economics); after-tax 1-year deposit about 4.3%
equity_return_base.note: Base case about 3 points over the after-tax safe rate, kept modest because the local index's 10-year record is mixed; diversified global funds are also widely held.

equity_return_high.sourceName: IGPA record high 58,749 in January 2026 (Trading Economics)
equity_return_high.note: High case: Chilean and global shares keep close to their strong 2023-2026 gains.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold USD price history (Trading Economics); CLP 994 per USD (SII, 27 Oct 2026)
gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold stalls after the 2025-26 rally and the peso firms with copper prices.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold USD price history (Trading Economics); Chile 3% vs US 2% inflation targets
gold_return_base.note: Base case: gold rises roughly with world inflation plus a little in dollars, and the peso loses about 1% a year against the dollar.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend in pesos.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: 30-89 day deposits 4.12% (Banco Central de Chile) less a little tax
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: short deposits only, with further rate cuts.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: 90-day to 1-year deposits 4.53% (Banco Central de Chile) less tax on the real part
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: term deposits after tax; tax applies only to real interest, so the after-tax rate stays close to the nominal one for most savers.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: 10-year peso government bond 6.00% (Banco Central de Chile daily bulletin)
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: locking in medium and long government bonds (through funds or brokers) at today's yields.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The CMF publishes insurance market statistics, but no industry-wide life claim settlement ratio was found (the CMF site could not be reached).

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life insurance is sold in Chile, but no regulator or other public table of premiums per CLP 1,000 of cover by age was found; only company quotes exist.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: No official figure for the typical out-of-pocket cost of a major private hospital stay was found; costs depend on FONASA or ISAPRE coverage.

health_premium_table.note: Private health insurance (ISAPRE plans and complementary policies) is priced per person in UF a month, not per sum insured; no public premium table per CLP 100,000 of cover exists.

oop_health_share.note: Out-of-pocket spending was 39.1% of current health expenditure in 2024 (latest available; older than 2025).

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: INE, IPC September 2026 bulletin: Salud division up 5.1% over 12 months
goal_inflation_health.note: Health prices rose 5.1% against 4.1% for all items; planning uses 5%, about 2 points above the 3% target, since medical costs rise faster over long periods.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: INE, IPC September 2026 bulletin: Educación division up 5.8% over 12 months
goal_inflation_education.note: Education prices rose 5.8% in the year to September 2026; planning uses 5%, about 2 points above general inflation.

life_expectancy.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_expectancy.note: Life expectancy at birth 81.7 years in 2026 (men 79.9, women 83.5), UN WPP estimate. World Bank 2024: 81.4.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_table_remaining.note: Remaining years from georank's expected age at death by current age (UN WPP 2026 estimate).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 21.2 (2025, World Bank), 33.1 (2040) and 66.9 (2065, populationpyramid.net/chile/2065/).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: ChileAtiende, Pensión de vejez del sistema de pensiones (AFP)
retirement_age_default.note: Legal pension age 65 for men and 60 for women in the individual-account system (DL 3.500); retiring is optional at that age and early retirement needs a pension of at least 12 UF.

retirement_age_government.sourceName: ChileAtiende, Pensión de vejez del sistema de pensiones (AFP)
retirement_age_government.note: Civil servants hired since 1981 contribute to the same AFP system, so the same pension ages of 65 (men) and 60 (women) apply; no separate civil-service pension age was found.

retirement_return_low.note: Low case: short deposits after small taxes, with rate cuts.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: 90-day to 1-year deposits 4.53% less tax on real interest (Banco Central de Chile; PwC)
retirement_return_base.note: Base case kept just below the after-tax 1-year deposit rate.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: 5-10 year peso government bonds 5.81-6.00% (Banco Central de Chile daily bulletin)
retirement_return_high.note: High case: a ladder of medium government bonds or UF-indexed annuities bought at today's yields.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if shares lag.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half shares at 7.5% and half safe fixed income at about 4.3% after tax.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning balanced mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.sourceName: ChileAtiende (Instituto de Previsión Social), Pensión Garantizada Universal (PGU)
old_age_allowance_monthly.note: PGU pays CLP 231,732 a month at 65-74 to people with a base pension up to CLP 789,139 (a smaller amount up to CLP 1,252,602); from 75 the maximum is CLP 250,275 under the 2025 pension reform. It is paid on top of other pensions and while still working.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: ChileAtiende (Instituto de Previsión Social), Pensión Garantizada Universal (PGU)
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Age 65 for men and women; not in the richest 10% of the population (pension targeting score), at least 20 years' residence since age 20 and 4 of the last 5 years, and a base pension of at most CLP 1,252,602.

gratuity_rule.note: Chile's Labour Code gives severance of 30 days' pay per year of service (capped at 11 years and 90 UF a month) only when the employer dismisses for business needs, not on retirement or resignation, so there is no retirement gratuity; the Labour Directorate page stating the scale could not be read.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: ChileAtiende, Pensión de vejez del sistema de pensiones (AFP)
public_pension_scheme.note: Compulsory individual-account system (AFP) for employees, with a new employer-funded social insurance component from the 2025 reform: pension age 65 (men) or 60 (women); the pension depends on the account balance, age and life expectancy, annuities are paid in inflation-indexed UF, and pensions are taxed as income.

savings_account.note: Mostly UF-indexed accounts with a small real rate; no published average rate.

fdr_1y.note: Also sold in UF (inflation-indexed) for terms of 90 days or more.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No retail government savings certificate or savings bond.

tbill_91d.note: No Treasury bills; central bank discount notes (PDBC) are sold to institutions only.

tbond_5y.localName: Bono de la Tesorería en pesos (BTP)
tbond_5y.note: Bought by individuals through brokers or bond funds.

tbond_10y.localName: Bono de la Tesorería en pesos (BTP)

equity_fund.localNameEn: Equity mutual fund or index fund (ETF)
equity_fund.note: Equity mutual funds and ETFs are widely sold to retail investors; voluntary pension savings (APV) carry tax relief.

gold.note: Buying physical gold is legal; there is no specific retail gold scheme.

insuranceComplaints.name: CMF, consultas y reclamos (Presentaciones CMF)
insuranceComplaints.note: Complain to the insurer first; then to the CMF. Health insurers (ISAPRE) are handled by the Superintendencia de Salud.

oldAgeAllowance.name: Pensión Garantizada Universal (PGU), Instituto de Previsión Social

depositInsurance.name: State deposit guarantee (Garantía estatal a los depósitos), explained by the CMF
depositInsurance.note: No separate insurer: the state guarantees term deposits of individuals up to 200 UF per bank per year.
